title: Relative Ranks
statement: Higher score means better placement. Places 1,2,3 are Gold Medal, Silver Medal, Bronze Medal; later places are decimal strings. Return each label at its ORIGINAL athlete index, not in sorted score order.
constraints: 1 <= score.length <= 10,000; scores are UNIQUE integers from 0 to 1,000,000.
Higher score means better placement. Places 1,2,3 are Gold Medal, Silver Medal, Bronze Medal; later places are decimal strings.
Return each label at its ORIGINAL athlete index, not in sorted score order.
hints: Sort athlete indices, not just scores, so you can restore original positions.
Walk indices by descending score and translate one-based placements to labels.
For each ranked index, write its medal or numeric rank string into answer[index].
Scores are unique, so there is no tie rule. Numeric placements must be strings, and the output order remains the input order.
editorial: Sorting indices separates rank order from output order. The original index is where each label belongs, regardless of the order in which ranks are assigned. The independent oracle counts how many scores are strictly larger for each athlete.

tests.explanation: These athletes are already in descending score order, so the labels are Gold, Silver, Bronze, "4", "5".
Placements in original order are 1,5,3,2,4. The score 9 gets Silver Medal at index 3, not at output index 1.
